# time

Types from the Go package `time` (a library PocketBase builds on), as JavaScript sees them: they turn up as values of [PocketBase's types](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase) and of hook events.

## time.Month

A Month specifies a month of the year (January = 1, ...).

Has everything <code>Number</code> has.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> | String returns the English name of the month ("January", "February", ...). |

## time.Weekday

A Weekday specifies a day of the week (Sunday = 0, ...).

Has everything <code>Number</code> has.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> | String returns the English name of the day ("Sunday", "Monday", ...). |

## time.Location

A Location maps time instants to the zone in use at that time.
Typically, the Location represents the collection of time offsets
in use in a geographical area. For many Locations the time offset varies
depending on whether daylight savings time is in use at the time instant.

Location is used to provide a time zone in a printed Time value and for
calculations involving intervals that may cross daylight savings time
boundaries.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> | String returns a descriptive name for the time zone information, corresponding to the name argument to `LoadLocation` or `FixedZone`. |

## time.Time

A Time represents an instant in time with nanosecond precision.

Programs using times should typically store and pass them as values,
not pointers. That is, time variables and struct fields should be of
type [`time.time`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), not *time.Time.

A Time value can be used by multiple goroutines simultaneously except
that the methods [`Time.gobDecode`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), [`Time.unmarshalBinary`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), [`Time.unmarshalJSON`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) and
[`Time.unmarshalText`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) are not concurrency-safe.

Time instants can be compared using the [`Time.before`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), [`Time.after`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), and [`Time.equal`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) methods.
The [`Time.sub`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) method subtracts two instants, producing a [`Duration`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration).
The [`Time.add`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) method adds a Time and a Duration, producing a Time.

The zero value of type Time is January 1, year 1, 00:00:00.000000000 UTC.
As this time is unlikely to come up in practice, the [`Time.isZero`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) method gives
a simple way of detecting a time that has not been initialized explicitly.

Each time has an associated [`Location`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timelocation). The methods [`Time.local`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), [`Time.uTC`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), and Time.In return a
Time with a specific Location. Changing the Location of a Time value with
these methods does not change the actual instant it represents, only the time
zone in which to interpret it.

Representations of a Time value saved by the [`Time.gobEncode`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), [`Time.marshalBinary`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), [`Time.appendBinary`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime),
[`Time.marshalJSON`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime), [`Time.marshalText`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) and [`Time.appendText`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) methods store the [`Time.location`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime)'s offset,
but not the location name. They therefore lose information about Daylight Saving Time.

In addition to the required “wall clock” reading, a Time may contain an optional
reading of the current process's monotonic clock, to provide additional precision
for comparison or subtraction.
See the “Monotonic Clocks” section in the package documentation for details.

Note that the Go == operator compares not just the time instant but also the
Location and the monotonic clock reading. Therefore, Time values should not
be used as map or database keys without first guaranteeing that the
identical Location has been set for all values, which can be achieved
through use of the UTC or Local method, and that the monotonic clock reading
has been stripped by setting t = t.Round(0). In general, prefer t.Equal(u)
to t == u, since t.Equal uses the most accurate comparison available and
correctly handles the case when only one of its arguments has a monotonic
clock reading.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|

| `appendFormat()` | <code>(b: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;, layout: string): string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> | AppendFormat is like [`Time.format`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime) but appends the textual representation to b and returns the extended buffer. |

| `equal()` | <code>(u: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime">Time</a>): boolean</code> | Equal reports whether t and u represent the same time instant. The zone begins at start and the next zone begins at end. If the zone begins at the beginning of time, start will be returned as a zero Time. If the zone goes on forever, end will be returned as a zero Time. The Location of the returned times will be the same as t. |
| `unix()` | <code>(): number</code> | Unix returns t as a Unix time, the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC. The result does not depend on the location associated with t. | `unixMilli()` | <code>(): number</code> | UnixMilli returns t as a Unix time, the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC. The result is undefined if the Unix time in milliseconds cannot be represented by an int64 (a date more than 292 million years before or after 1970). The result does not depend on the location associated with t. |
| `unixMicro()` | <code>(): number</code> | UnixMicro returns t as a Unix time, the number of microseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC. The result is undefined if the Unix time in microseconds cannot be represented by an int64 (a date before year -290307 or after year 294246). The result does not depend on the location associated with t. |
| `unixNano()` | <code>(): number</code> | UnixNano returns t as a Unix time, the number of nanoseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC. The result is undefined if the Unix time in nanoseconds cannot be represented by an int64 (a date before the year 1678 or after 2262). Note that this means the result of calling UnixNano on the zero Time is undefined. The result does not depend on the location associated with t. |

| `truncate()` | <code>(d: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration">Duration</a>): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime">Time</a></code> | Truncate returns the result of rounding t down to a multiple of d (since the zero time). The rounding behavior for halfway values is to round up. If d <= 0, Round returns t stripped of any monotonic clock reading but otherwise unchanged. |

## time.Duration

A Duration represents the elapsed time between two instants
as an int64 nanosecond count. The representation limits the
largest representable duration to approximately 290 years.

Has everything <code>Number</code> has.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> | String returns a string representing the duration in the form "72h3m0.5s". Leading zero units are omitted. As a special case, durations less than one second format use a smaller unit (milli-, micro-, or nanoseconds) to ensure that the leading digit is non-zero. The zero duration formats as 0s. |
| `nanoseconds()` | <code>(): number</code> | Nanoseconds returns the duration as an integer nanosecond count. |
| `microseconds()` | <code>(): number</code> | Microseconds returns the duration as an integer microsecond count. |
| `milliseconds()` | <code>(): number</code> | Milliseconds returns the duration as an integer millisecond count. |
| `seconds()` | <code>(): number</code> | Seconds returns the duration as a floating point number of seconds. |
| `minutes()` | <code>(): number</code> | Minutes returns the duration as a floating point number of minutes. |
| `hours()` | <code>(): number</code> | Hours returns the duration as a floating point number of hours. |
| `truncate()` | <code>(m: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration">Duration</a>): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration">Duration</a></code> | Truncate returns the result of rounding d toward zero to a multiple of m. If m <= 0, Truncate returns d unchanged. |
| `round()` | <code>(m: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration">Duration</a>): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration">Duration</a></code> | Round returns the result of rounding d to the nearest multiple of m. The rounding behavior for halfway values is to round away from zero. If the result exceeds the maximum (or minimum) value that can be stored in a [`Duration`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration), Round returns the maximum (or minimum) duration. If m <= 0, Round returns d unchanged. |
| `abs()` | <code>(): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timeduration">Duration</a></code> | Abs returns the absolute value of d. As a special case, Duration(`math.minInt64`) is converted to Duration(`math.maxInt64`), reducing its magnitude by 1 nanosecond. |
